dedupe_keys.name: peer ground motion database nga west2 nga east and the peer lbnl simulated ground motion database

description: The PEER Ground Motion Database is a web tool of the Pacific Earthquake Engineering Research Center, a nine-campus centre headquartered at UC Berkeley, for searching, selecting and downloading recorded earthquake ground motions, widely used to select and modify records for analysing models of buildings, bridges and other facilities and cited in the NEHRP Recommended Provisions. Coverage: NGA-West2 holds a very large worldwide set of records from shallow crustal earthquakes in active tectonic regions, with extensive metadata on distance measures, site characterisation and sources, close to the set behind the 2014 NGA-West2 ground motion models; NGA-East holds over 29,000 two- and three-component records from 81 events and 1,379 stations in central and eastern North America since 1988 (M above 2.5, distances to 1,500 km), with time series, 5%-damped pseudo-spectral accelerations for periods of 0.01 to 10 s and Fourier amplitude spectra; a separate simulated ground motion database (SGMD) with Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory is offered at sgmd.peer.berkeley.edu. Format and access: web search and download of unscaled, unrotated records with a scaling tool whose factors come with the metadata; free, with registration using a university or company email. Licence: not stated; the site cites copyright issues for its download limits. Caveats: downloads are capped at about 200 records every two weeks and 400 a month; from 2 July 2026 all accounts were reset to one-year memberships that must be renewed. Simulation uses: input motions for nonlinear time-history analysis of buildings, bridges and lifelines in seismic fragility and resilience studies. Related records: the records are commonly run in OpenSees (model-opensees), also from PEER.
